newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks edge up on speculation.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks edge up on speculation.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher despite continued profit-taking, as some investors speculated among liquid growth counters, brokers said.
The all share index closed 1.46 points up at 633.74. Hatton National Bank rose 2.50 rupees to 255, NDB two to 195.
"Activity was centred around liquid growth stocks because these are the counters where you can take profit, and trading positions," said Namal Kamalgoda, a fund manager at CTC Eagle Fund Management.
Korea Ceylon, Bogala, Grain Elevators, Sampath, Lion Brewery and Tea Smallholder, were the focus of a lot of attention, brokers said.
Turnover was 41 million rupees on 1.7 million shares, with parcels of 732,000 Horana Plantations and 147,700 Lion Brewery, the day's bigget trades.
"Though there were a few making stretegic investments, the majority were either taking profit or speculating," said Deva Ellephola a trader at brokerage Jardine Fleming.

Blue chip John Keells Holdings fell 21.25 rupees to 175, as the share adjusted to its ex-bonus price. The company announced a one for seven bonus issue in December. The share traded on Monday for the first time since going ex-bonus on January 20.
